title: Salzburg and Münster books and German-speaking diocesan Mass propers

traditions.label: Salzburg local Mass books
traditions.scope: The 1498 pre-Tridentine Salzburg print, the 1605 Roman-based Salzburg missal and later local Mass-proper printings, with the Roman basis and particular feasts kept distinct.
traditions.coverage_note: The 1596 papal permission is reported by an archive museum; its original instrument, the 1605 body and exact replacement of preceding Salzburg texts remain to be checked.

traditions.label: Münster diocesan missal
traditions.scope: The 1632 Münster missal and a bound 1784 supplement expressly addressed to it.
traditions.coverage_note: Original 1632 decree and the 1784 supplement text remain unread; the indexed book states do not establish a complete revision sequence.

traditions.label: German-speaking Swiss diocesan propers
traditions.scope: German local Mass and lectionary supplements to the postconciliar Roman books.
traditions.coverage_note: St Gall identifies the 1976 volumes as current official local Mass texts; the original volumes and approval leaves have not been inspected.

traditions.label: Cologne postconciliar propers
traditions.scope: Latin and German particular Mass and lectionary components of the Roman books for the Archdiocese of Cologne.
traditions.coverage_note: The 2026 official directorium calls the 2002 components binding; original 2002 approval and book pages remain uninspected.

traditions.label: Speyer postconciliar propers
traditions.scope: Particular calendar, Mass propers and lectionary components for the Diocese of Speyer.
traditions.coverage_note: The 2023 lectionary reports separate 1971, 1972 and 1975 authority events; original instruments and the first proper book are not inspected.

traditions.label: Aachen postconciliar propers
traditions.scope: Particular Mass propers of the Diocese of Aachen as adjuncts to the postconciliar Roman Missal, kept separate from any medieval or early-modern local use of the same see.
traditions.coverage_note: Only the Roman confirmation of 11 July 1975 (Prot. 697/75) is dated, from the Congregation's published summary; its proper calendar is among those confirmed on 15 November 1972 (Notitiae 9, 1973, p. 127), which is not a separate stage here. No proper book, decree text or prayer has been inspected.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00032991 canvas 11 and canvases 13–24
evidence.claim: Salzburg-notula Ordo and complete calendar inspected.

stages.label: Missale Salisburgense, Roman basis with Salzburg feasts
stages.date_label: 1605 printed and distributed
stages.scope: Salzburg missal as a local edition with Roman basis and particular feasts, according to an archive museum account.
stages.witness_label: Archive of the Archdiocese of Salzburg copy pictured by DomQuartier
stages.summary: Wolf Dietrich printed and distributed 1,228 copies. The institutional account identifies the Roman Missal as basis and says Salzburg local feasts were added. It separately reports Clement VIII's 1596 permission.

evidence.locus: Wolf Dietrich räumt auf, archive-object caption and paragraphs following it
evidence.claim: The institution identifies the 1605 book, reports its circulation, Roman basis, local feasts and earlier papal permission.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb11057620 canvas 1 (title), canvas 7 (Rubricae generales Missalis) and canvas 54 (September calendar)
evidence.claim: The title states the missal was restored according to the rite and custom of the Roman Church with approval of the Apostolic See and issued by authority of Archbishop Wolf Dietrich; the calendar uses Roman grading while keeping Salzburg feasts. The front matter carries the Roman general rubrics.

stages.limitations: The original 1596 act is uninspected and no mandate leaf was found in the digitised copy. Apart from the September calendar, neither title nor retrospective description proves exact prayer changes or a direct descent from a particular Roman edition. The 1605 Mass bodies are uninspected.
stages.reception: Reported publication and circulation in Salzburg, not a measured date of first or universal use.

stages.summary: The Congregation for Divine Worship confirmed the Latin and German texts of Cologne's Proprium Missarum (with the Liturgia Horarum) on 11 November 2002 (Prot. 2282/99/L); the official directorium lists the 2002 Latin/German Mass-proper book as a binding part of the archdiocesan Missal and the 2002 Lectionary proper as a binding Lectionary component.

evidence.locus: Notitiae 39 (2003), printed p. 21 (PDF p. 22), Dioeceses, entry Köln, Germania
evidence.claim: The Congregation confirmed the Latin and German Proprium Missarum and Liturgia Horarum of Cologne on 11 November 2002, Prot. 2282/99/L.

evidence.locus: PDF p.26, printed XXVIII, item h; p.27 item m
evidence.claim: The 2026 authority list identifies the 2002 proper components and their binding diocesan status.

stages.limitations: The confirmation is known from the Congregation's published summary, which names the Proprium Missarum and Liturgia Horarum but not a Lectionary; the Lectionary component rests on the 2026 Directorium alone. The original 2002 books, the decree text, exact prayers and effective date are not inspected. This is a local component state, not a distinct whole Order of Mass or continuity claim from the historical Cologne use.
stages.reception: Binding status is documented for the archdiocese by 2026; first-use date not established.

stages.witness_label: Approval references on p.2 of the Diocese of Speyer's 2023 Lectionary
stages.summary: The Sacred Congregation for Divine Worship's published summary lists Spirensis among the dioceses whose proper Mass texts were confirmed by the collective decree of 11 July 1975 (Prot. 697/75); the 2023 Speyer Lectionary cites the same protocol and date. The earlier calendar approvals are a separate stage.

evidence.locus: Printed p. 231 (PDF p. 29), Regiones Linguae Germanicae, entry Spirensis
evidence.claim: Prot. 697/75 of 11 July 1975 is a collective particular decree confirming the proper Mass texts of twenty-three dioceses listed under Regiones Linguae Germanicae, Spirensis among them.

evidence.locus: PDF p.2, Approbation und Konfirmation, lines 5–14
evidence.claim: The diocese's own book cites the 11 July 1975 confirmation under Prot. 697/75.

stages.limitations: Lectionary claim narrowed (2026-10-22): the 2023 Lectionary's approval page, as read on 2026-10-20, associates the 1975 confirmation with Mass and Lectionary proper texts, but the Congregation's published summary of Prot. 697/75 names only textus proprii Missarum. This stage therefore carries the propers component only (the summary's silence does not show that no Lectionary texts were confirmed); when a Speyer proper Lectionary was first approved remains unestablished. The 2023 page could not be re-read on 2026-10-22 because the diocesan host timed out. The decree text, the confirmed texts and the first proper book are uninspected; no exact before/after change or first celebration is claimed.
stages.reception: Approval only; first use of the first edition is not independently dated.

stages.label: Speyer proper calendar confirmed with the German-language diocesan calendars
stages.date_label: 15 November 1972 Roman confirmation (Prot. 2069 series), as reported in Notitiae 9 (1973) and the 2023 Speyer Lectionary, after the bishop's approval of 3 November 1971
stages.scope: Roman confirmation of the diocesan proper calendar of Speyer, one of 41 German-language diocesan calendars confirmed together.
stages.witness_label: No calendar book inspected; Notitiae 9 (1973), printed pp. 126–127, and the 2023 Speyer Lectionary p. 2
stages.summary: The Congregation's summary records that on 15 November 1972 the proper calendars of the German-language dioceses, Spirensis among them, were confirmed under Prot. n. 2069; the 2023 Speyer Lectionary gives the same date with Prot. 2069/71 after Bishop Wetter's approval of 3 November 1971. The date clash recorded in batch 4 is resolved: the 21 September 1972 entry under Prot. 2069/71 (Notitiae 8, 1972, p. 361) is the separate confirmation of the common regional calendar for the German-language area.

evidence.locus: Printed pp. 126 (last entry) – 127 (PDF pp. 12–13), section VI, entry Regiones linguae Germanicae, Spirensis in the list on p. 127
evidence.claim: Collective confirmation of the German-language diocesan proper calendars on 15 November 1972, Speyer included.

evidence.locus: PDF p.2, Approbation und Konfirmation, lines 5–14
evidence.claim: The diocese's book dates the bishop's calendar approval to 3 November 1971 and the Roman confirmation to 15 November 1972 (Prot. 2069/71).

evidence.locus: Notitiae 8 (1972), printed p. 361
evidence.claim: The 21 September 1972 entry under Prot. 2069/71 confirms the common regional calendar, a distinct act from the diocesan calendar confirmation.

stages.limitations: The calendar itself, its feasts and ranks, and the original instruments are uninspected. The 1971 episcopal approval is known only from the 2023 book. The identity of 'Prot. n. 2069' with the 2069/71 file is inferred from the shared number, region and date.
stages.reception: Approval only; first use of the calendar is undated.

transitions.summary: The January and September calendars of the 1605 Roman-restored Salzburg missal replace the local grading with Roman double and semidouble ranks, add Roman sanctoral entries and drop several local saints, while keeping the Salzburg feasts of 24–26 September.

changes.before: Grades expressed as festum, bini and ix lessons; Michael entered as Michaelis archangeli.
changes.after: Grades expressed as Dupl., Semidupl. and commemorations, with daily octave days of the Nativity of Mary; 29 September entered as Dedicatio S. Michaelis.

evidence.locus: MDZ bsb00022261 canvas 13
evidence.claim: The September page of the 1506 Vienna Salzburg missal keeps the 1498 saints and festum/bini/ix grading, so the September differences listed here are not present in that print.

transitions.limitations: January and September only. The 1506 Vienna print's September page agrees with 1498, so these September differences are absent from that print; the 1507 and 1510 prints, the 1596 permission and any intervening books are uncollated, so when between 1506 and 1605 the differences entered is unknown, and this page does not show that other months or the Mass bodies changed at the same time. Absence from one calendar page does not prove absence from the sanctorale. The 1506 print's January page was not compared, so the January differences can only be placed between 1498 and 1605.
